findings.title: English reference file path is derived with an unsafe, unanchored regex
findings.body: The verifier maps a translated file to its English reference by applying replaceAll to the full absolute path with an unanchored locale-suffix pattern. The pattern is also written with an unescaped hyphen and does not explicitly cover numeric locale tags. If the path contains another matching underscore segment, or if a locale such as messages_es_419.properties is used, the computed English file can be wrong or missing. This can make the verifier compare against the wrong bundle or fail with a RuntimeException.

findings.title: ChoiceFormat normalization removes HTML from sanitized input
findings.body: normalizeValue() replaces the entire ChoiceFormat block with '...' before OWASP sanitization for keys starting with linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit and for error-invalid-multivalued-size. Any HTML placed inside the choice alternatives is therefore removed before sanitization and never checked. A malicious translation could use something like '{2,choice,0#<script>alert(1)</script>values}' and bypass the HTML verification, while the message may still be rendered as HTML in emails or login pages.

findings.title: Anchor tags are stripped before sanitization and are not validated
findings.body: santizeAnchors() removes anchor tags that match the English source before policy.sanitize() is called. When verifying the English file itself, the value and the English value are identical, so all anchors are removed before the sanitizer ever sees them. As a result, an English source string containing an unsafe anchor such as <a href='javascript:alert(1)'> passes verification. The logic also does not detect translations that omit an anchor present in the source.

findings.title: Illegal HTML diff computation can throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException
findings.body: The code strips common prefix and suffix characters before printing the differing substring, but it never ensures that the prefix and suffix do not overlap. If sanitized and value differ by inserted characters while still sharing beginning and ending characters, start can become greater than length - end, causing substring() to throw. This would abort verification instead of reporting the offending key.

findings.title: Account UI message changed from i18next syntax to Java MessageFormat/ChoiceFormat
findings.body: This account-ui message file uses i18next/React syntax throughout, for example other error-* keys use {{0}} and some messages use Trans tags like <0>. The changed error-invalid-multivalued-size now uses Java MessageFormat/ChoiceFormat syntax with {0} and {2,choice,...}. The account UI will not evaluate that server-side Java format, so users are likely to see raw placeholders or broken pluralization.

findings.title: Admin UI message changed from i18next syntax to Java MessageFormat/ChoiceFormat
findings.body: The previous value used {{0}}, matching the admin UI's i18next-style interpolation. The new value uses Java MessageFormat/ChoiceFormat syntax with {0} and {2,choice,...}. If this key is rendered by the admin UI frontend, the placeholders and choice expression will not be processed, producing a broken user-facing validation message.

findings.title: Lithuanian account message replaced with Italian text
findings.body: The Lithuanian account console message totpStep1 was changed to the Italian sentence 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:' instead of Lithuanian. Lithuanian users will see Italian text in the account UI.

findings.title: Lithuanian login message replaced with Italian text
findings.body: The Lithuanian login message loginTotpStep1 was changed to the Italian sentence 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:' instead of Lithuanian. Lithuanian users will see Italian text on the login page.

findings.title: Simplified Chinese account message uses Traditional Chinese characters
findings.body: The zh_CN account console message totpStep1 was changed to '在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：', which uses Traditional Chinese characters. messages_zh_CN is Simplified Chinese, so this is inconsistent with the locale and the rest of the file.

findings.title: Danish HTML email contains stray 'n' before 'Hvis'
findings.body:
identityProviderLinkBodyHtml contains the paragraph '

nHvis du ikke vil forbinde disse konti...'. The leading 'n' is a typo and should be '

Hvis du ikke vil forbinde disse konti...'. This text is visible in the HTML email.
